items.review_rationale: Read the fraction-field universal property over integral domain D with field F and injective embedding, requiring a unique compatible field homomorphism into each other containing field K.

references.phrase: field F and arbitrary field K
injective ring map i:D to F
references.context: One-to-one unital homomorphism embedding D as a subring of field F.

references.phrase: universal commutative triangle h composed with i equals j
references.context: For every injective embedding of D into any field K, a factorization through F exists.

references.phrase: unique field homomorphism h:F to K
references.context: Single multiplicative/additive unit-preserving field map commuting with D embeddings.

references.phrase: universal property equivalent to concrete fractions
references.disposition: This alternative presents the same fraction-field meaning without redefining it via an unnecessary self-link.

items.review_rationale: Read integer as quotient of ordered pairs of natural numbers by formal-difference equivalence, with coordinate equation a+d=b+c; do not confuse with field fractions.

references.context: On N by N, (a,b) equivalent to (c,d) precisely if a+d=b+c.
Set of all equivalence classes of natural-number pairs for the formal-difference relation.
Informal interpretation of ordered pair as the difference represented by its integer class.

references.disposition: The quotient construction uses the zero-inclusive natural-number model available in the current independent inventory.

items.review_rationale: Read ring of integers as the integer set equipped with ordinary addition and multiplication, distinct from a specific class representation and with ring axioms implicit.

references.context: Well-defined associative commutative binary addition with additive identity and inverses on integer elements.
Associative distributive multiplication with multiplicative identity 1 on integer elements.

references.disposition: Ring Z has its usual unital commutative structure and not all nonzero elements have multiplicative inverses.

items.review_rationale: Read a right R-module over possibly nonunital associative ring via abelian additive group and right scalar action satisfying both distributivities and right associativity; no unit axiom added.

references.phrase: right scalar action M x R to M

references.context: The right scalar action is additive in its M input.
The right scalar action is additive in its R input.
Compatibility of right action with ring multiplication, in the correct right-sided order.

references.disposition: The right-module definition does not impose m1=m without a specified unit-preserving convention.
